title: QICT: Receiver Distinguishability and the Spectral Derivation of Standard-Model Structure
content: This paper formulates Quantum Information Copy Time (QICT) as a relational receiver–spectral con-struction in which an operational receiver quotient constrains a finite spectral triple and its admissible finite operators. Under the explicitly stated representation-theoretic, reality, grading, order-zero/order-one, minimality and receiver-selection hypotheses, the construction reduces the finite algebra to AF ≃ C ⊕ H ⊕ M3(C) and selects the primitive endpoint denominator q = 14 within the declared QICT endpoint-sieve and holographic-ground rule. The Majorana pushout gives qν = 21 under the stated transfer condition qν/q = 3/2, while the three-dimensional C3 Fourier sector yields an exact tribimaximal ultraviolet boundary with sin2 θ13UV = 0. The primitive register angle θreg = π/21 is kept distinct from the physical PMNS reactor angle. The one-loop minimal SMνR evolution is shown not to generate the observed nonzero reactor angle, providing a quantitative no-go and falsification target for the minimal flavour sector. For the explicitly specified canonical Hermitian three-link holonomy and positive heat-kernel spectral action, the exact stationary analysis gives Φ⋆ = 0, π and hence JCP = 0 and δCP = 0 or π; a nonzero parameter-free leptonic CP prediction therefore requires an additional receiver-derived, non-commuting finite operator whose coefficients are fixed before minimization. The electroweak and neutral numerical ledgers retained in the manuscript are explicitly classified as conditional finite-threshold or illustrative spectral completions whenever the supplementary closure does not independently fix the required matching data. The manuscript consequently separates structural theorems, QICT dynamical axioms, conditional numerical constructions, and falsification targets, while retaining the receiver, finite-algebra, flavour, neutral, electroweak, temporal-spatial and experimental material of the integrated construction.
